welcome.label: Welcome · Next Year’s Trophy

parts.label: 🏅 A new trophy
parts.title: Order one for next year
parts.body: Mr. Ortiz wants a NEW trophy. He wrote down exactly what it must do.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a paper cup and a metal spoon.) If I needed a cup for hot soup, which would you pick? What about a spoon for stirring?

[ON SCREEN: A new trophy]
You found the real Duck Derby trophy. Now Mr. Ortiz wants a brand new one for next year.

[ON SCREEN: The order form]
It has to survive rain, not break if a little kid drops it, and weigh under 500 grams.

[ON SCREEN: Four designs]
The engraver sent four designs. Only one fits every need. Read the case file just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · take it apart (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Snap two blocks or two markers together, then pull them apart.) Together… apart. Did I just lose anything?

[ON SCREEN: Predict]
The whole robot weighs 60 grams. Will the pile of parts weigh more, less, or the same? Lock in your prediction first.

[ON SCREEN: Take it apart]
Then drag each part onto Scale 2 and watch the adding tape. Answer the question, and Clue one is yours.

part1.label: Part 1 · sticker every property (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Hold up a rubber band and stretch it, then drip a drop of water on it.) It bends. And water rolls right off. So which group does rubber belong in?

[ON SCREEN: The sticker sheet]
Both! Give every material every sticker that fits. Each card shows how many it needs. A wrong sticker bounces off, so read why.

part2.label: Part 2 · the job test rigs (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🔩 Steel
parts.title: Can steel win them all?
parts.body: Strong and heavy. Is that always best?

part2.script:
(Pretend to open an umbrella, then pretend it is made of heavy metal and can barely lift it.) Hmm. A steel umbrella. Great idea?

[ON SCREEN: The rigs]
Pick a job, read what it needs, drag in a material, and run the test. If it fails, swap and run again.

[ON SCREEN: Steel]
Try steel in every rig. Does the strongest material win every job?

part3.label: Part 3 · the 412-gram puzzle (wow)

parts.label: 🔧 The bench
parts.title: The real trophy in pieces
parts.body: Tap each part. The tape adds it up.

part3.script:
(Point at a pile of LEGO or pencils on your desk.) A pile always LOOKS smaller than the whole thing.

[ON SCREEN: The bench]
The engraver took the real trophy apart, and Mr. Ortiz is worried some brass went missing. Tap every part on the bench, and watch the total. Remember: the whole trophy weighed 412 grams.

explore.label: Part 4 · the drip and bend lab (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Drip one drop of water on a paper towel and one on a piece of foil.) Look! One drinks it up, one won’t.

[ON SCREEN: Drip it]
Test all five swatches. Drip water, watch, and tap what you saw. Then bend each one.

[ON SCREEN: Your table]
Your results build a classification table. Read it to find which materials pass BOTH tests. That’s Clue four.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Which design?
parts.body: Add up each design. Check every need. Pick the one that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to work
rows: Choose a material for a job at home

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four designs, three needs. Add up each design’s parts, check every need, and pick the one that fits all four clues. Then watch for a late note from Mr. Ortiz!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next, two short answers. For Part C, pick a job at home, like a raincoat or a dog bowl, and choose its material. Then sketch and label it. Last comes your CER about steel.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “There’s one best material for everything: steel.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Flex your arm like a strongman.) Steel is strong. Steel is tough. So steel is the best at everything… right?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says steel is the best material for everything. You tested steel today, in four different jobs.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🏅 Your specimen
parts.title: The new trophy design
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: Magnets
parts.body: Attract, repel, and test them yourself.

closing.script:
(Hold up an imaginary trophy and read an imaginary engraving.) Next year’s winner will hold a trophy YOU designed.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the new trophy design goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: One more wow]
Did you see the glowing NASA tile? Every material in that photo was picked for a job.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week: magnets!

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
